 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:

On 09-12-2024 at about 6.30 p.m., the petitioner was riding TVS XL motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-EQ-5493 along with his wife, from Tavarekere to Yelachaguppe Village, Hakki-Pikki Colony via Kengeri, on the left side of the road.

When he reached near Smashana, on Tavarekere-Kengeri road, at that time the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989, drove the same from Yelachaguppe side, in a rash and negligent manner, with high speed and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Supra Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as coolie and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Tavarekere Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 281 and 125(a) of BNS.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.MX828741, in respect of car bearing No.KA-41-MB-9989 and its validity from 30-12-2023 to 29-12-2024.
However, the liability/obligation of this respondent shall be strictly subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It has denied the manner of accident and also involvement of the insured vehicle in the Mareppa vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119513471/

sentences.text: It has contended that, the petitioner was riding the alleged TVS XL bearing No.KA-04- EQ-5493 without knowledge of riding, without wearing helmets, in a rash and negligent manner and without possessing valid vehicle documents and he had suffered self accident.
The insured vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident.

If it is proved that the insured vehicle is involved in the alleged accident and drivers of both vehicles are responsible for the alleged accident, the liability is be reduced to the extent of the negligence of the petitioner.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner and the driver of the insured vehicle were not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the class of their vehicles at the time of the alleged accident.
The respondent No.2 has knowingly entrusted the insured vehicle to the driver, who had no valid and effective driving licence.
Therefore, the insured has consciously breached the terms and conditions of the policy and absolved this respondent from indemnifying the liability, if any, under the alleged cause of action.

Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2,
as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non- compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 09-12-2024 at about 6.30 p.m., near Smashana, Yalachaguppe, Kengeri- Tavarekere road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-41-MB-9989 ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Pramod Kumar M., as P.W.2.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-41-MB-9989 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.2, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-EQ- 5493 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989.
Further it has contended that, the offending car is not at all involved in the alleged accident.
But, the respondents No.1 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any oral evidence, nor it has produced any documentary evidence to establish the above contentions.
Even, the respondent No.1 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989 and dashing the same to oncoming motorcycle bearing No.KA- 04-EQ-5493 of the petitioner from opposite direction.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04- EQ-5493 himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of the Kengeri-Tavarekere road, near Smashana, Yalachaguppe village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, in between offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989 and oncoming motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-EQ-5493 of the petitioner.
As per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report,
marked as Ex.P.3, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary,
Ex.P.13 case- sheet, Ex.P.14 x-ray and Ex.P.15 recent examination report, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained Mareppa vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 4 April, 2026

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained above injuries in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the said medical records of the petitioner.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 09-12-2024 at about 6.30 p.m., near smashana, Yalachaguppe Village, Kengeri-Tavarekere road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-41-MB-9989.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained compound fracture of femur M/3rd - L/3rd of right femur and fracture of lateral condyle of left tibia and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.

loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

sentences.text: Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.12.
As per Ex.P.12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-01-1992.
The accident has taken place on 09-12-2024 at about 6:30 p.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 33 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered compound fracture of femur M/3rd - L/3rd of right femur and fracture of lateral condyle of left tibia.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries sustained by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability to the extent of 21.5% to the whole body from right lower limb.

Further, the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary, Ex.P.13 case- sheet, Ex.P.14 x-ray and Ex.P.15 recent examination report clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
The P.W.2 has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants with exchange nailing with bone grafting.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 09-12-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 20-01- 2026, which is after lapse of one year and one month from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, at the time of discharge the condition of the petitioner was stable and if the petitioner undergoes follow up treatment there are every chances of reducing the complaints to the petitioner stated in his affidavit, the fracture of left tibia is united and at the time when he examined the petitioner the wounds were also healed.

Further he has admitted that, after future surgery there are every chances of uniting of fracture of right femur and after union of said fracture there are every chances of reducing the complaints stated in his affidavit.
Further he has clearly stated that, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner,
duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
20. The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as coolie and he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Further he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.

sentences.text: Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB- 9989.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the driver of offending vehicle by name Hemanth N. Murthy S/o P. Narasimha Murthy was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA0220050025432 to drive the said vehicle.
The policy issued by the respondent No.1 bearing No.MX828741, in respect of offending car, was valid from 30-12-2023 to 29- 12-2024.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 09-12-2024.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.2.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-41-MB-9989 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,82,191/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization,
from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.10,82,191/- (Rupees ten lakh eighty two thousand one hundred and ninty one only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the said medical records of the petitioner.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
